commit.message:
Aggregate the audio mute state across PeerConnections (#336)

Two PeerConnections from one factory share one audio processing module
(APM) and one audio device module (ADM). Today `MuteStream` computes
"all streams muted" over its own channel only, and writes the result to
both shared modules. So if an app mutes the track of one PeerConnection,
capture processing stops and the microphone mutes for every
PeerConnection. On Apple with voice processing on, the other
PeerConnection then sends silence. Part of
livekit/client-sdk-swift#1213.

## Change

The middle two commits are upstream cherry-picks, with the upstream
messages and a short conflicts note:

- 725a4522d1 ([CL
508963](https://webrtc-review.googlesource.com/c/src/+/508963)) computes
the APM mute across all send channels of the voice engine.
- 6b54e7c1aa ([CL
512880](https://webrtc-review.googlesource.com/c/src/+/512880)) removes
two getters that the first change made unneeded.

Fork commits:

- Fix stale voice engine test fixtures. Test-only. At the base, 250 of
353 selected cases fail.
- Drive the fork ADM mute (`SetMicrophoneMute` and stop-on-mute) from
the same engine aggregate. The engine reads the device state before each
write. A stream without a source counts as unset, which keeps the fork
rule "Don't mute when removing audio stream". Stream removal, a detached
or closed source, and channel destruction can stop recording but never
start it.
- Release the APM mute when no configured stream remains. Upstream keeps
the last value, so a call that ends muted leaves capture processing off.
With #333 the engine stays initialized between calls, so local capture
now gets frames with no PeerConnection, and this release keeps those
frames processed. This commit is separate, so it can be dropped.

The branch has `m150_release` merged in, including #333 and #296. The
merges had no conflicts.

## Verified

- `rtc_media_unittests
--gtest_filter='*WebRtcVoiceEngine*:*AudioProcessingController*:*AudioProcessingOptionsResolver*'`
passes on each commit alone, also in a build with `rtc_disable_logging =
true`. At the head: 400 passed, 0 failed, 3 skipped. The skips are the
real-APM tests in their no-APM case. Each new regression test fails
without its product change. A few tests only pin behavior that the base
already had.
- `peerconnection_unittests
--gtest_filter='*PeerConnectionFactory*:*MediaEngine*'` passes at the
head, including the two tests from #333.
- macOS, LiveKit Swift SDK, two rooms in one process, a real microphone.
On 150.7871.05, muting the track in one room gave 0 capture
post-processing callbacks in 4 s, and the subscriber of the other room
received about -106 dBFS. With this branch, the callbacks continued
(about 400 in 4 s) while either room stayed unmuted, and stopped when
both rooms were muted.
- iPhone 17 Pro Max, iOS 27, two PeerConnections on one factory (see the
review below): muting one track kept about 99 callbacks per second and
left the microphone unmuted. On `m150_release` it gave 0 and muted the
microphone.
- macOS, built from the branch with #333 merged: after a call that ended
muted, the APM and the microphone were both unmuted, and local recording
with no room got 413 to 427 callbacks in 4 s. Every build without #333
got 0 there.

## Not done yet

- No test on Android, Linux or Windows. Stop-on-mute, the default
outside Apple, has unit tests only.
- The engine expects the ADM mute mode to stay the same at runtime. A
switch away from stop-on-mute does not restart recording.
- The Swift SDK writes the APM mute directly in
`AudioManager.startLocalRecording()`, which bypasses the engine cache.
Coordinating such direct writes with the engine is follow-up work.

---------

Co-authored-by: Tore Rudberg <trudberg@google.com>
Co-authored-by: Sam Zackrisson <saza@webrtc.org>
